prompt.context: The client is a regional retail bank. Recently, it has begun facing threats from Internet-based financial services firms and other non-traditional firms. Deposits are declining and the bank has approached us with a strategy to grow the bottom line.
prompt.question: Walk me through some of the issues that you consider and work streams you would set up in coming up with some recommendations.

clarifying_info.q: Can you tell me more about the client – their customers, brand, and history?
clarifying_info.a: The client is a well-established bank based in New England. They have about 3 million customers and an acquisitions strategy that has been reasonably successful. They offer a slew of products including deposits/savings accounts, small investments, credit cards and mortgages. However, they have been laggards in eBanking.

clarifying_info.q: How do customers perceive the client's brand?
clarifying_info.a: They are a reputed and established firm, known for trust and security. They have chosen to remain a regional bank and consequently customers are quite loyal.

clarifying_info.q: What competitive threats are they facing?
clarifying_info.a: Competition has intensified both from traditional firms, particularly other regional banks, and also from new, non-traditional firms. Internet-based firms are able to offer a better perceived value proposition to customers and the client feels that there is a strong threat of losing loyal customers.

clarifying_info.q: Is the client looking for new product ideas?
clarifying_info.a: That would surely be one area to explore. It is not clear if that is the primary focus of the client.

framework: 1. Client Strengths: Assess brand equity, customer reach (3M customers), product breadth (deposits, investments, credit cards, mortgages), and regional loyalty
2. Competitive Assessment: Evaluate threats from traditional regional banks and Internet-based non-traditional firms; analyze value propositions and eBanking gap
3. Capabilities & Growth Options: Design the capabilities needed to grow the bottom line; use a product-channel value-vs-convenience matrix to prioritize options

questions.prompt: How would you help the client prioritize the various product and channel options?
questions.guidance: Identify the major product lines (e.g., banking/savings, brokerage, retirement accounts). For each product, map the available channels (branch, Internet, etc.). For each product-channel combination, conduct a value-vs-convenience analysis to segment offerings by service quality and value proposition. This surfaces where to invest to improve the client's competitive position.

questions.prompt: If the client currently makes $100 million in profit with 3 million customers and wants to reach $120 million in profit, what strategic growth paths exist and which would you recommend?
questions.guidance: Plot revenue per customer on the Y-axis and number of customers on the X-axis. Current state is Point 1 ($100M profit, 3M customers). Three paths to $120M profit exist: Point 2 (increase revenue per customer with same customer base – loyalty/cross-sell strategy); Point 3 (reduce customer count while increasing revenue per customer – attrition/cherry-picking strategy); Point 4 (increase both customer base and revenue per customer – acquisitive + loyalty strategy). The recommended path is Point 4 as it leverages the client's brand trust and customer loyalty while expanding the base.

math.setup: Profit = Revenue per customer × Number of customers. Current: $100M profit, 3M customers. Target: $120M profit. Three paths along the $120M isoprofit curve.
steps: Point 2: Same 3M customers, higher revenue per customer (deeper relationships/cross-sell)
Point 3: Fewer customers, higher revenue per customer (eliminate unprofitable customers)
Point 4: More than 3M customers AND higher revenue per customer (acquisitive + deepened relationships)
math.answer: Point 4 is preferred: grow the customer base while simultaneously deepening relationships to enhance loyalty.

recommendation: Recommend the Point 4 strategy: grow the customer base beyond 3 million while deepening existing customer relationships to increase revenue per customer
Leverage the client's established brand equity (trust, security, regional loyalty) to differentiate from Internet-based competitors
Accelerate eBanking capabilities to close the competitive gap with non-traditional firms while retaining loyal customers
risks: eBanking investment is costly and the bank is already a laggard – execution risk is high
Aggressive customer acquisition may dilute brand or attract unprofitable customers
Deepening relationships requires cross-sell capability and data analytics the bank may lack
next_steps: Conduct a detailed product-channel value-vs-convenience analysis to identify highest-priority investment areas
Benchmark eBanking capabilities against leading Internet banks to define the capability roadmap
Develop a customer segmentation model to identify highest-value customers for loyalty programs and acquisition targeting
